derivation_notes: The parent's single exponential establishment factor is replaced by a broader delay-response law in which cumulative effective establishment rises as x/(1 + x) with x = tau/tau_est, representing heterogeneous transit and attachment delays across inhaled infectious units. This preserves bounded monotone infection probability while changing the short-to-intermediate duration curvature of the scored mapping itself.
change_summary: Changed the assumption that all infectious units share one sharply defined establishment phase, replacing it with a broader saturating establishment response. The consequence is a different tau-curvature of infection risk when tau is comparable to tau_est, while retaining the same long-duration monotone saturation structure.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: Finite transit/attachment/penetration delay is represented by one common exponential establishment-lag factor with a single characteristic time tau_est.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Heterogeneity in airway deposition depth, mucus transport, attachment, and penetration creates a distribution of establishment delays across inhaled infectious units within an episode.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The successor is a law refinement of the establishment kernel; there is no exact parameter-only identity, but it is intended as the next broader-delay approximation replacing the parent's single-phase kernel in the same fixed-input setting.

response_change.parent_relation: For fixed q and attenuation parameters, infection pressure grows from an onset-lag-suppressed approximately quadratic rise at very short tau toward an approximately linear-in-tau accumulation tempered by a single attenuation factor, so the dose effect mainly rescales one shared time-course shape.
response_change.child_relation: Replace the single establishment-lag phase by a broader transit-time assumption so early contributors arrive over a distribution of delays rather than one characteristic delay, changing the short-to-intermediate tau curvature of cumulative infection pressure while preserving monotone saturation of p_inf.
response_change.observable_effect: At fixed D and q, short episodes no longer all collapse onto the same single-timescale onset shape: compared with the parent, intermediate durations can show a more gradual turn-on after the earliest suppression, which changes the tau-curvature of p_inf without requiring nonmonotonicity.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Most visible when tau is of order tau_est (x_lag around 0.3 to a few) and att_load is not already very large, so the episode samples the onset regime rather than only the long-time attenuated regime.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, the mechanism appears as systematic deviation from a single universal onset-lag shape across short and intermediate tau. In holdout, the same distributed-delay effect extends to broader tau/tau_est ranges while preserving the same long-duration parent-like behavior.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the distributed-delay shape back to the single-timescale limit so effective establishment approaches the original 1 - exp(-tau/tau_est) factor.
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Heterogeneity in airway deposition depth, mucus transport, attachment, and penetration creates a distribution of establishment delays across inhaled infectious units within an episode.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is structurally harder than a coefficient-only correction because it changes the shape of the establishment kernel itself, introducing a different saturating onset law in tau/tau_est rather than merely rescaling infection pressure.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: Finite transit/attachment/penetration delay is represented by one common exponential establishment-lag factor with a single characteristic time tau_est.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: Establishment delays are broadly distributed, so cumulative effective establishment during the episode follows a saturating delay-response rather than one single-phase exponential turn-on.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: The child is intended as a broader-delay continuation of the same mechanism; the parent is recovered conceptually by narrowing the delay distribution back toward the original single-phase establishment law.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Holding D, q, and environmental conditions fixed while varying tau, the parent gives one shared onset-lag shape through 1 - exp(-tau/tau_est), whereas the child gives a different saturating onset kernel ((tau/tau_est)/(1 + tau/tau_est)). The scored mapping p_inf(tau) therefore shows changed short-to-intermediate curvature when tau is comparable to tau_est, especially before attenuation load becomes dominant.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot generally match both the earliest suppression and the broader intermediate turn-on across these conditions because the parent has only one characteristic lag-shape family, controlled by tau_est as a location/scale parameter. Refitting beta_inf, tau_est, or attenuation parameters rescales or shifts the onset but does not create the altered curvature of the establishment kernel itself.

evolution_plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, the mechanism appears as systematic deviation from a single universal onset-lag shape across short and intermediate tau. evolution_plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the distributed-delay shape back to the single-timescale limit so effective establishment approaches the original 1 - exp(-tau/tau_est) factor.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes all inhaled pathogens share one sharply defined establishment timescale, which can make the onset of effective infectivity unrealistically single-phase.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: Finite transit/attachment/penetration delay is represented by one common exponential establishment-lag factor with a single characteristic time tau_est.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Heterogeneity in airway deposition depth, mucus transport, attachment, and penetration creates a distribution of establishment delays across inhaled infectious units within an episode.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's single-phase establishment-lag assumption rather than add a wholly new process. The parent already includes finite onset suppression through tau_est, but it forces every infectious unit to contribute through the same exponential turn-on shape. Biologically, deposited pathogens reach productive establishment over a spread of delays because of heterogeneous landing sites and traversal paths. Vary tau while holding q, D, and environment fixed: the parent predicts one shared onset curvature governed only by tau/tau_est, then attenuation takes over. A child with distributed establishment delays changes the mapping from tau to p_inf itself, not merely an auxiliary interpretation: at the same D and q, short-to-intermediate episodes can accumulate effective infectivity more gradually than the parent's single-phase rise, while remaining nondecreasing and bounded. This contrast is observable when tau is comparable to tau_est and before gamma_att*tau*(1 + delta_dose_att*D) becomes so large that late-time attenuation masks the onset structure. Refitting all existing parent parameters cannot generally reproduce both the earliest suppression and the broader intermediate turn-on with one shared parameter set, because the parent has only one characteristic lag shape; changing tau_est rescales the onset location but does not introduce an independently adjustable onset curvature. The refinement naturally reduces back to the parent in the narrow-delay limit.

selected_embedding_pattern.description: Use a finite-capacity, saturation, threshold, or regime-transition response.

scenario_text: Estimate the probability that a susceptible person becomes infected during a single exposure episode. The independently varied conditions are inhaled pathogen dose, exposure duration, and host susceptibility, while environmental conditions remain fixed. Infection risk rises with cumulative exposure but approaches an upper bound because probability cannot exceed certainty. The benchmark targets the episode-level risk rather than subsequent disease progression.
